privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How SI processes input locally, handles optional saved data, and connects only for user-initiated app updates.
privacy.intro: Your words belong on your Mac. This policy explains the local input method, the data you can choose to keep, and the separate network requests involved in this website and software updates.

sections.title: 1. Input stays on your Mac
paragraphs: SI processes composition and generates candidates locally using resources on your Mac. Typing needs no internet connection or account. Keystrokes, composition, committed text, personal phrases, learned preferences and input history are not sent to a server. SI has no analytics, cloud inference or raw-keystroke logger. Separately enabled Input History can retain each SI submission locally.

SI does not read documents or clipboard text, request Accessibility or Input Monitoring permissions, or use a global event tap. The host application still receives text you commit and handles it under its own privacy practices.

sections.title: 2. You choose what SI remembers
paragraphs: Language and feature preferences stay in macOS UserDefaults. Personal Learning and Input History have independent switches and both default to off; language choices and one feature never enable the other. Personal Learning is global, without per-app learning controls. Retired consent/history/app-exclusion settings cannot enable the new history feature.

Personal Learning keeps consumed spelling, output/language identity, aggregate usage/correction counts, strength, last-use time and the current deliberate choice. One nonfirst choice leads the next exact normalized spelling, after explicit personal-phrase pins. Accepting the first choice counts usage only; every three corrections also add one frequency point up to 32. Strength does not decay and rows do not expire by age. Up to 5,000 rows remain, with least-recently-used capacity eviction.

When enabled, Input History saves each SI submission with exact source spelling, submitted text, time, a distinct event identity, language and commit type. Repeats remain separate. Original English, personal phrases, punctuation and automatic confirmations are included; prefixes record only their submitted portion. History is retained indefinitely until deletion, without age/count eviction or the learning vocabulary cap. It is for local viewing/search, not ranking, completions or automatic training/upload.

Cancelled/unconfirmed compositions, standalone passthrough keys, text outside SI, direct-input apps and secure input are excluded. Secure event input cannot identify every sensitive field. No document, clipboard, URL or recipient is read. Past input and retired history archives are not imported; migration of old app archives to global learning still drops retired history fields.

Users can explicitly export all saved history as one JSONL file to a selected destination. Export opens the save panel directly, without backup/training choices or training-permission fields. SI does not send the file or start training. After the owner manually shares it, receiver tools can validate version/count/checksum and restore every event or prepare unreviewed training observations from the same file. Local deletion cannot erase exported or shared copies.

sections.title: 3. Personal phrases are separate
paragraphs: Phrases you explicitly add keep your input code, output, language, pin setting, and identifier locally until you delete them, with a 1,000-phrase limit. They are separate from automatic learning. Import and export are explicit actions; you choose the export destination. Exported files contain personal data and remain under your control.

sections.title: 4. Inspect, disable, and delete
paragraphs: Settings → Personal Learning → Manage Learning Data offers global inspection, Forget and clear. Settings → Input History offers independent recording consent, paged viewing/search, individual Delete and Clear Input History. Turning a switch off stops new recording while keeping saved data and finishing accepted queued writes. History clear also discards pending retries, and older writes cannot restore cleared rows. Learning, history and phrases are deleted independently; removing one category does not erase copies in another.

History uses a separate local SQLite file without age/count eviction. Files/directories have owner-only permissions, but are not encrypted; other software running as you, administrators or backups may access private text. Writes and bounded page reads run off the main actor. Open/save errors pause recording and show recovery controls. Pending failed writes are only in memory and require retry before quitting. Normal termination waits for queued writes; forced termination, disk failure or unretried errors may lose unsaved entries.

The separate retired shared-learning archive remains inactive and is never automatically loaded, imported or deleted; Delete Old Shared Learning Data explicitly removes it. SI deletion does not erase exports, external backups or forensic filesystem remnants. Independent direct-input app rules stop conversion and recording in those apps.

sections.title: 5. Local storage and its limits
paragraphs: App vocabulary and personal phrases are stored in SI’s Application Support directory. Private archives use owner-only file permissions and atomic replacement, but SI does not encrypt them. Other software running as your user, administrators, or backups may be able to access them. Expiry cleanup runs at startup and during daily maintenance. Storage and migration failures are shown in Settings.

sections.title: 6. Optional software updates
paragraphs: The app’s only network feature is a user-initiated Check for Updates action using Sparkle. It requests the public HTTPS appcast from downloads.caterm.com; an update archive is requested if you choose to download/install. Automatic checks, automatic installation, and system-profile submission are disabled. No vocabulary download is needed while typing.

These requests expose ordinary connection metadata, including IP address and HTTP user agent, to the download service. They do not include input text, personal phrases, learned preferences, or history. Sparkle may retain updater preferences, last-check information, and cached downloads locally. Visiting the website or downloading installers also involves ordinary web requests; those are separate from local typing.

sections.title: 7. This website and external services
paragraphs: This static website includes no analytics, advertising trackers, cookies, browser storage, remote fonts, or input-upload forms. Its animation uses fixed synthetic examples and does not capture what you type. The website host and download service receive ordinary connection metadata, such as IP address and request information, when serving pages or files; this policy does not promise that those services keep no access logs.
Links to GitHub, including public feedback, are subject to GitHub’s privacy practices. Share only non-sensitive synthetic examples when reporting an issue.

sections.title: 8. Questions and changes
paragraphs: For privacy questions or corrections, contact the project maintainers through the repository. GitHub issues are public: do not include private input, phrase exports, or personal archives. Changes to this policy will appear here with an updated date. The implementation and its documented limits remain available in the source.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: SI development-preview terms, GPLv3 software rights, installation responsibilities, and links to the full license.
terms.intro: SI is free, open-source software in development preview. These terms explain the website and preview; the software license governs your rights to use, modify, and redistribute SI.

sections.title: 1. Scope
paragraphs: These terms describe the SI website and the development-preview software distributed by this project. They do not add restrictions to, replace, or take away rights granted by the GNU General Public License version 3 (GPLv3). Where a software-license question arises, the applicable license text controls.

sections.title: 2. Open-source license
paragraphs: SI is distributed under GPLv3. You may run, study, modify, and redistribute it under that license’s conditions. If you redistribute the software, follow the applicable source-code, notice, and licensing requirements in the full license. Included third-party components and dictionary data retain their documented licenses and attribution requirements.

sections.title: 3. Development-preview status
paragraphs: SI currently supports English and Simplified Chinese with bounded decoding. Vocabulary coverage, candidate quality, ranking, and host-app compatibility remain under development. Website demonstrations are scripted illustrations, not promises of particular candidate ordering, accuracy, latency, or compatibility. Planned features may change and are not a commitment to delivery.

sections.title: 4. Installation and use
paragraphs: Choose the installer for your Mac’s architecture and follow the installation guide. Save your work before the installer’s final Log Out step. Review committed text before relying on it, and keep appropriate backups. You control your enabled languages, personal phrases, and optional app vocabulary. Review the Privacy policy for retained data and deletion controls.

The input method works offline after installation. Downloads, manual update checks, and external project links require a connection and may have their own service terms. No account is required for local typing. Automatic software update checks and installation are disabled.

sections.title: 5. Warranty and liability
paragraphs: SI is supplied without warranty to the extent permitted by applicable law, as described in GPLv3 sections 15 and 16. Those sections govern the software’s warranty disclaimer and limitation of liability. Nothing on this page excludes rights or liabilities that applicable law does not allow to be excluded.

sections.title: 6. External services and feedback
paragraphs: The website links to hosting, download, and repository services. Their own terms and privacy policies apply to those services. Public issue reports should contain only non-sensitive examples. Contributions are handled under the repository’s contribution guidance and existing licenses.

sections.title: 7. Changes and contact
paragraphs: The website and preview may change as development continues. Updates to these terms will be dated on this page and do not revoke software rights already granted under GPLv3. For questions, contact the project maintainers through the repository. Do not put private text or local data archives in public issues.
